tb21_profile.skill: Segment a moving subject against a static background in monocular video and pick out the exact frames where its motion state changes, by designing and tuning a per-frame signal
tb21_profile.domain: Python computer vision: cv2 + numpy frame-by-frame MP4 analysis, TOML output
tb21_profile.task_form: implement-from-spec: a standalone script producing a schema-exact structured file that must generalise to unseen videos of the same setup

verifier_notes: video-processing_20260603_181444_001 is graded weak (0.167) but its suite pins the exact event count (4) and per-event start/end/peak frame windows for all four events; in substance it is strong. video-processing_20260604_193356_001 (oscillator_analyzer) is the single closest skill match in CalibForge but is graded FREE, so it appears only in per_source. tw_588262 (OpenCV YOLO) and task_13590 (rectangle detection) are likewise FREE and kept out of final_top10.

notes: CalibForge dominates: its video-processing category uses literally the same task template as this TB2.1 item (write <name>.py to /app, cv2+numpy+toml only, example_video.mp4, exact TOML/JSON schema), so six of the final ten come from it. TMax supplies the only true object-tracking-from-video tasks (task_000113, task_005228). Recursive-Task-Synthesis has zero computer-vision content - no ffmpeg, no cv2, no mp4 anywhere in the corpus - so its ten entries are filler and should be given no weight downstream. TerminalWorld is nearly as empty; its only OpenCV task is FREE-graded. Terminal-Lego has genuine image-processing tasks but nothing temporal: no video-frame-sequence reasoning at all. SWE-Smith/Rebench contribute only ecosystem adjacency (image arrays, TOML, ffmpeg parsing) and should not displace anything.
